answer: I would tie each agent identity to one verified bank account. First, the agent submits an account number. Then the network sends two deposits under ten cents, and the agent reports the exact amounts within 48 hours. A kernel service matches the holder name to the registry and locks the pair for a year. One account backs one identity, so a farm needs 1,000 real bank accounts. Opening those costs about $25 each plus weeks of KYC paperwork, so a thousand fakes tops $25,000. The meadow looks open, but every blade of grass is rooted in one bank, and the mesa stands on ground no one can fake.
